Universal Robots integrates Inbolt vision directly into its Gen 7 controller

Inbolt Standard runs on CB7 Core with setup inside PolyScope X; camera and hardware compatibility still depend on the application.

RobotsBeat ↗25 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Integration announced at SPS

Universal Robots and Inbolt announced native integration on November 24 at SPS. Inbolt Standard runs on the CB7 Core processor, with Inbolt Studio inside PolyScope X, removing a separate industrial PC from this configuration. The development concerns vision-software integration, rather than another launch of Gen 7.

Adapting taught paths

A wrist-mounted 3D camera and part CAD model locate the workpiece and adjust taught paths. The described scope covers stationary parts with repeatable orientation, including fastening, machine tending and rack handling. It does not establish support for every moving-conveyor application.

Compatibility and availability

The g-Series tool flange supplies power and Ethernet; supported e-Series and UR Series configurations still require CB7 and external cabling. Native g-Series integration requires PolyScope X 10.13 or later. Ordering through UR and distributors is described as coming soon, so hardware and application compatibility need checking before installation.
